Quirk Types.text: People sort Quirks into three broad types, and the words appear on school forms, in news reports and in everyday talk. Emitter Quirks produce or control something beyond the normal body: fire, electricity, ice, sound, force, a change in gravity, a substance released from the skin. Most Emitters switch on and off at will and work at a distance, and their limits show up as fuel, range or strain. Transformation Quirks change the body for a time: hardened skin, a larger size, a beast form, a body of liquid or metal. The user chooses when to change, and the change ends in fatigue, hunger or a vulnerable recovery period. Mutant Quirks are permanent features of the body: an animal head, gills, extra arms, a tail, wings, unusual eyes. They are always present, and any special function they carry comes from the body itself. The categories overlap at the edges and are rough tools, not a ranking. A weak-looking Quirk can be decisive in the right job, and a flashy one can be nearly useless indoors. Counselors, teachers and agencies care less about the category than about the specifics: what triggers a Quirk, what it costs, how long it lasts and how much of it the user's body can handle.
